title: A 32-bit write to a general-purpose register clears the upper half
summary: Writing EAX clears the upper 32 bits of RAX. Writing AX or AL leaves higher bits unchanged.
applies: 64-bit mode for x86-64; Intel SDM Volume 1 and Volume 2
detail: If RAX is originally all 1, RAX will be 1 after executing mov eax,1; after executing mov ax,1 with the same initial value, RAX will be ffffffffffff0001.
boundary: This rule specifies integer general-purpose register destination operands; the analogy does not apply to all vector register writes.
relevance: When reconstructing a register snapshot, distinguish between zero extension and partial coverage after narrow writes.
